name: Jolla Jolla
pros: Wi-Fi support (Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n, hotspot) for data-free browsing and connectivity
2 MP camera capable of capturing good photos for its release era
Snapdragon 400 chipset provides balanced everyday performance
Li-Ion 2100 mAh battery offers solid operating endurance for daily use
cons: Limited RAM (1 GB RAM) constraints modern multitasking
Standard charging speeds without ultra-fast charging support

reviews.title: Solid performance for its 2013 launch era
reviews.body: Picking this up around its release period, the Sailfish 1, up to 2.0 experience felt snappy and responsive for the price tier. The 2 MP camera delivered reliable shots in outdoor lighting.

reviews.title: Reliable battery and daily usability
reviews.body: The Li-Ion 2100 mAh power cell paired with Jolla's software tuning easily lasted through a full work day with mixed web browsing, calls, and media playback.

reviews.title: Refined hardware styling and build
reviews.body: The physical chassis of the Jolla Jolla feels well-balanced in hand. Its 131 x 68 x 9.9 mm (5.16 x 2.68 x 0.39 in) make it easy to hold during long daily sessions.

reviews.title: Great value for the hardware specifications
reviews.body: For the price point, getting Snapdragon 400 performance alongside 16GB storage, microSDHC made the Jolla Jolla an easy recommendation among rivals in 2013.

reviews.title: Smooth day-to-day software responsiveness
reviews.body: Operating on Sailfish 1, up to 2.0, the user interface is intuitive with smooth system transitions. Core apps and browsing run without noticeable stutter.

reviews.title: Dependable display and audio clarity
reviews.body: The screen (Li-Ion 2100 mAh, removable (7.98 Wh), 4.5", 540x960 pixels) produces vibrant colors for video streaming, and call clarity through the earpiece is crystal clear.

reviews.title: A well-rounded package from Jolla
reviews.body: Overall, the Jolla Jolla proved to be a durable and well-engineered mobile device representing Jolla's design philosophy nicely.
